slots.name: iconProps
slots.doc: The item icon, when it has one. The chevron is NOT exposed: motion animates it.

slots.name: itemProps
slots.doc: Every item in the list. It spreads over ALL of them, not over one.

slots.name: labelProps
slots.doc: The item label, inside the button.

slots.name: panelProps
slots.doc: The disclosure panel. It lives inside a `Collapse`, so that is what governs its height.

slots.name: triggerProps
slots.doc: The button that opens and closes. It already carries the `aria-expanded` and the `aria-controls`.

own.name: children
own.doc:
The glyph, and the whole of the button's content. It is `aria-hidden`, so the control has no
accessible name until you give it one — an `aria-label` here is not optional.

own.name: color
own.doc:
The scale the variant draws from. Name the scale and let the variant pick the steps out of it;
pinning a step here is what breaks the hover and active states, which are derived from it.

own.name: disabled
own.doc:
Blocks the press and drops the hover and press animation with it. No need to pair it with
`loading`, which already disables on its own.

own.name: glass
own.doc:
Overrides the glass step the variant's recipe asks for. It is ignored in three cases that are
not errors: a variant whose recipe has no glass, a theme with `effects.glass.enabled` off, and
a `color` that is not one of the theme's scales — a hex or a role path never takes glass.

own.name: gradient
own.type: { from: ColorExtended; to: ColorExtended; deg?: number; animate?: boolean; }
own.doc:
Read only by `variant="gradient"`, where it replaces the theme's pair. `deg` is 135 if you do
not say otherwise, and `animate` needs this override to exist at all — it does nothing over the
theme's own gradient.

own.name: loading
own.doc:
Lays a spinner over the button, marks it `aria-busy` and disables it. The icon dims in place
rather than being swapped out, so the button holds its square while the work runs.

own.name: size
own.doc:
The button's square, in both axes at once. It is the tap target, so anything below `md` on a
touch surface has to be given room by its container instead.

own.name: variant
own.doc:
The recipe the theme resolves background, border, glow and glass from, all at once. A row of
icon buttons reads as one control strip only if they share it.

slots.name: iconProps
slots.doc:
Wrapper for the icon. With `loading` it dims, which is how the button makes room for the spinner
without changing size; the spinner itself has no slot, because it is the mechanism of the animation.

own.name: children
own.doc: What is pinned to the viewport — a scroll-to-top, a floating action, a cookie bar.

own.name: position
own.doc:
Which corner it sits in, as viewport insets. Setting `top` and `bottom` together stretches it
rather than centring it, so pick one of each axis. Numbers are pixels; strings pass through.

own.name: visible
own.doc:
Whether it renders at all. False unmounts it outright — there is no transition here, so wrap it
in a `Transition` if it should fade rather than vanish.

own.name: withinPortal
own.doc:
Renders through a portal, out of the containing layout, which is what keeps an ancestor's
`transform` or `overflow` from capturing a fixed position. Turn it off only when the affix must
stay inside a region that manages its own stacking.

own.name: zIndex
own.doc:
Where it sits in the stack. It starts high enough to clear page content but below the overlay
range, so a modal covers it — which is the behaviour a floating action wants.

slots.name: actionsProps
slots.doc: The action row. Only with `actions`. The close button does not land here and has no slot: `withCloseButton` and `closeLabel` govern it.

slots.name: bodyProps
slots.doc: The column that groups title, message and actions. Always rendered.

slots.name: iconProps
slots.doc: The glyph. Only rendered with `icon`, and it is `aria-hidden`: the text is what informs.

slots.name: messageProps
slots.doc: The message, which is `children`. It does not exist without them.

slots.name: titleProps
slots.doc: The title. Its `id` is what names the alert through `aria-labelledby`, and it is written AFTER the slot. Only rendered with `title`.

own.name: className
own.doc: Composes with the classes `Box` computes instead of replacing them.

own.name: component
own.doc:
The element it paints, and the seam where a router plugs in: pass your framework's link
component (`component={NextLink}`) and its own props travel through untouched. It is why the
core carries no router dependency.

own.name: external
own.doc:
Opens in a new tab and adds `rel="noopener noreferrer"` in the same move — the two go together
so an external target can never reach `window.opener`. Both are spread before the rest, so an
explicit `target` or `rel` of your own still wins.

own.name: inherit
own.doc:
Takes family, size, weight and line height from the parent instead of the `Text` defaults. For
text that must sit inside a heading or a button without breaking its type.

own.name: lines
own.doc:
Clamps the text to this many lines with an ellipsis. Beats `truncate`, and only applies above
zero. Needs a width to work against: inside a flex child, that usually means `miw={0}`.

own.name: truncate
own.doc:
Cuts the text to a single line with an ellipsis. Ignored when `lines` is set, which does the
same thing over several lines. The full text stays in the DOM, so it is still read aloud.

own.name: underline
own.doc:
When the underline shows. It is on always because the link has to be tellable from body text
without relying on colour; `"hover"` and `"never"` move that job onto something else, and the
surrounding design has to provide it.

own.doc: Composes with the classes `Box` computes instead of replacing them.

own.name: gradient
own.type: { from: ColorExtended; to: ColorExtended; deg?: number; animate?: boolean; } | GradientRole

slots.name: scrimProps
slots.doc:
The veil that dims the gradient. Only rendered with `scrim` greater than 0, which is where its
opacity comes from; the slot is what lets you tint it another colour without forking. The
drifting layer has no slot: it is the mechanism of the animation.

own.name: backdrop
own.doc: Decorative layer behind everything: this is where a `StarField` lives.

own.name: contentWidth
own.doc:
Bounds the rail grid — bar and content together — and centres it. Only the surfaces stay
full-bleed. Rail layout only.

own.name: mainRef
own.doc: The `main` is what scrolls in the rail layout; it is exposed so you can hook a parallax background to it.

own.name: railCollapse
own.doc:
What the rail does when the viewport stops fitting it (ADR-153). `"mini"` shrinks it to icons
below `laptop` and lays it out as a bottom bar below `tablet`. `"hidden"` withdraws it below
`laptop` and reserves no space for it — the shell cannot know its links are reachable, so pass
this only when another surface below that point carries them. Rail layout only.

own.name: scrollShadow
own.doc: Shadow sail at the start of the scrolling area; it appears under the chrome, not over it.

own.name: scrollShadowOffset
own.doc: The height the sail sticks from: use it to keep it beneath sticky chrome.

own.name: sidebar
own.doc: Full-height bar. Its presence switches the shell to the rail layout.

own.name: sidebarCollapsed
own.doc: Third rail state: the bar shrinks to `sidebarMiniWidth` and its labels are hidden.

slots.name: chromeProps
slots.doc: The top chrome band. Only exists in the rail layout, and only with a `header`.

slots.name: mainProps
slots.doc: The `main`. In the rail layout it is also what scrolls; its ref goes separately, through `mainRef`.

slots.name: scrollShadowProps
slots.doc: The shadow sail at the start of the scrolling area. Rail layout only, and only with `scrollShadow`.

slots.name: skipProps
slots.doc: The skip-to-content link, visible only when focused. It exists in both layouts.

own.doc: Composes with the classes `Box` computes instead of replacing them.

own.name: component
own.doc: The element it paints.

own.name: ratio
own.doc:
Width divided by height — `16 / 9` for video, `1` for a square. It reserves the height from the
width before the content loads, which is what keeps an image or an iframe from shifting the
page as it arrives.

own.name: alt
own.doc:
The image's alt text, and the accessible name of the whole avatar when there is no image. It
falls back to `name`; with neither, the avatar says nothing at all — which is what you want
beside a name already written out, and not what you want when it stands alone.

own.name: children
own.doc:
Replaces the initials — a glyph, a status mark. It never shows over an image, so it is the
fallback's fallback and not a layer on top.

own.name: color
own.doc:
The scale the fallback draws from. Deriving it from the name is the consumer's job — the same
`color` here gives every avatar in a list the same tint.

own.name: name
own.doc:
Where the initials come from: the first letter of the first and last words, uppercased. It also
names the avatar when there is no `alt`.

own.name: radius
own.doc: How round it is. `"sm"` and `"md"` are what turn it into a squircle for a team or an org.

own.name: size
own.doc:
The avatar's square, as a control step or as any length. Unlike the rest of the sizes here it
takes a raw value, which is what lets it line up with a row of arbitrary height.

own.name: src
own.doc:
The picture. A load failure is remembered for the life of the component, so it falls back to
the initials once and does not flicker between the two on later renders.

own.name: variant
own.doc:
How the fallback is filled. It only ever shows when there is no image, so it dresses the
initials and nothing else.

slots.name: imageProps
slots.doc: The image. Only rendered with a `src` that has not failed to load; on failure the initials take over.

own.name: aria-label
own.doc:
Names the set, which also makes it a `group` for assistive tech. Without it the avatars are
announced one after another with nothing saying they belong together.

own.name: children
own.doc: The avatars, overlapped in the order given: the first sits on top.

own.name: max
own.doc:
How many avatars are shown before the rest become a count. The overflow avatar is added by this
component, so do not leave a `+N` of your own among the children.

own.name: size
own.doc:
The square every avatar in the set takes, overriding their own. It also sets the overlap, which
is derived from it.

own.name: spacing
own.doc:
How far each avatar slides over the one before it. Left out it is 30 % of `size`, so the overlap
scales with the set instead of needing a new value per size.

own.name: total
own.doc:
The true size of the set, when it is larger than the children you passed. This is what makes the
count honest for a list that was paginated before it got here — without it the count can only
describe the avatars actually rendered.

own.name: children
own.doc:
The label. A badge is a `span` with no role of its own, so this text is all a screen reader
gets — a status shown by colour alone does not reach one.

own.name: color
own.doc:
The scale the variant and the dot draw from. It is also the whole semantic signal of a status
badge, which is why the label has to repeat it in words.

own.name: dot
own.doc:
Puts a coloured dot before the label, taking the 600 step of `color` regardless of how pale the
variant is. It is the status cue that survives a `"light"` badge on a busy row.

own.name: fullWidth
own.doc: Stretches the pill to its container instead of hugging the label.

own.name: leftSection
own.doc: An adornment before the label. It is `aria-hidden`, so it can only repeat what the label says.

own.name: radius
own.doc: How round the pill is.

own.name: rightSection
own.doc:
The same after the label, but this one is NOT `aria-hidden` — it is read out, which is what
makes it the place for a count or a dismiss control rather than a decorative glyph.

own.name: size
own.doc:
Height, padding and type of the pill together. It does not follow the text it sits beside, so a
badge inside small print has to be stepped down by hand.

own.name: variant
own.doc:
How the pill is filled. `"light"` is the tinted wash that sits in a table or a list without
competing with the row; the solid ones pull enough attention to read as a control.

slots.name: dotProps
slots.doc: The colour dot. Only rendered with `dot`; its colour comes from the scale, not from the stylesheet.

slots.name: leftSectionProps
slots.doc: Wrapper for `leftSection`.

slots.name: rightSectionProps
slots.doc: Wrapper for `rightSection`.

slots.name: actionsProps
slots.doc: Wrapper for the actions, when there are any.

slots.doc: Envoltorio del contenido.

slots.doc: Wrapper for the icon, when there is one.

own.name: cite
own.doc:
The attribution, set apart under the quote in a `cite`. Nothing renders there without it, so
styling the slot through `citeProps` alone will not bring the line back.

own.name: className
own.doc: Composes with the classes `Box` computes instead of replacing them.

own.name: color
own.doc:
The accent, drawn from the 500 step of this scale. It tints the rule down the leading edge and
the `icon` with it — the quote's own text keeps reading as body copy either way.

own.name: component
own.doc:
The element it paints. It is a real `blockquote` by default, which is what marks the passage as
quoted rather than merely indented.

own.name: icon
own.doc:
An opening glyph. Its presence is what switches the layout to two columns, and it is rendered
`aria-hidden`, so it can only ever decorate the quote — never carry part of it.

slots.name: citeProps
slots.doc: The attribution. Only rendered with `cite`, and it goes in a `cite`.

slots.name: contentProps
slots.doc: The box wrapping `children` and the attribution. Always rendered.

slots.name: iconProps
slots.doc: The glyph. Only rendered with `icon`; it is `aria-hidden`, and its presence switches the layout to two columns.

own.name: blur
own.doc:
How far what is behind is blurred. `md` is the operational ceiling; anything above belongs to
the occasional full-screen overlay and nowhere else. `"none"` drops the effect and leaves the
tint alone.

own.name: center
own.doc:
Centres the content. Passing `children` turns it on anyway, so this only decides anything for a
layer that carries none.

own.name: children
own.doc:
What rides on top of the blur. Passing anything also takes the layer out of `aria-hidden`:
empty, it is invisible to assistive tech, which is what a bare blur should be.

own.name: color
own.doc:
The tint laid over the blur. It defaults to the base surface so the layer reads as the page
fading out rather than as a colour arriving.

own.name: fixed
own.doc:
Covers the viewport instead of the nearest positioned ancestor. Without it the layer only covers
a region that is already positioned — over a static parent it will spill.

own.name: opacity
own.doc:
How much of the tint lands. It is deliberately low, because here the blur is what hides the
content. When the blur cannot run — `blur="none"`, or a theme with glass off — the veil is
forced up to 0.94 instead, so the layer never stops concealing what is behind it.

slots.name: contentProps
slots.doc:
The box that centres `children`. It does not exist without children, and without them the whole
layer becomes `aria-hidden`. The veil has no slot: it is the effect, and `blur`, `color` and
`opacity` govern it.

own.doc: Composes with the classes `Box` computes instead of replacing them.

own.name: component
own.doc:
The element it paints. Everything else about `Box` is style, so this is what decides its
semantics: without it you get a `div`, which is right for a wrapper and wrong for anything a
screen reader should announce. The DOM props it accepts follow from this.

own.name: collapseFrom
own.doc: How many items it takes before the middle ones collapse. `0` turns collapsing off.

slots.name: currentProps
slots.doc: The current crumb, which carries `aria-current` and is not a link.

slots.name: expandProps
slots.doc: The button that reveals the hidden crumbs. It only appears when the trail collapses.

slots.name: itemProps
slots.doc: Every crumb. It spreads over ALL of them, including the ellipsis one.

slots.name: linkProps
slots.doc:
The navigable crumbs. It does not land on the current one. Their element comes from the
`component` of each item, or from its `href`: with `href` it is an `a`, without it a `button`.
It does not go through `Box`, so it does not accept style props.

slots.name: listProps
slots.doc: The list.

slots.name: separatorProps
slots.doc: The separator. It spreads over all of them; the last one is not rendered.

own.name: closeLabel
own.doc: The name it takes while open, swapped in alongside `aria-expanded`.

own.name: color
own.doc:
The bars' colour. A role path like the default resolves straight to that token; naming one of
the theme's scales instead takes its 600 step.

own.name: defaultOpened
own.doc: Where the state starts when nothing controls it. Ignored the moment `opened` is passed.

own.name: disabled
own.doc: Blocks the press, so the state can only be moved from outside.

own.name: onChange
own.doc:
Fires with the state the button is moving TO, in both modes — so it is the change hook when
uncontrolled and the only way to move when controlled.

own.name: opened
own.doc:
The open state, controlled. Passing it takes the state away from the button for good: it stops
tracking its own, and `onChange` becomes the only thing that can move it.

own.name: openLabel
own.doc:
The button's accessible name while closed — three bare bars have no text of their own. Say what
the press does, not what the state is: `aria-expanded` already carries the state.
It is English by default (ADR-120); translate it at the call site.

own.name: showBelow
own.doc: The breakpoint below which the button appears; always, by default.

own.name: size
own.doc:
The button's box, and with it how far the bars travel as they cross. The two are tied on
purpose: a bar that moves the wrong distance does not land on a clean X.

own.doc:

pinning a step here is what breaks the hover and active states, which are derived from it.

own.name: disabled

own.name: onOpenChange

own.name: openDelay

own.name: accentColor
own.doc: The tint of the occasional accent star, which also carries a wider glow.

own.name: accentEvery
own.doc:
One star in every this many takes `accentColor`. It feeds the generator, so changing it does not
merely recolour the accents — it picks a different set of them.

own.name: aurora
own.doc:
Adds the slow drifting colour blobs behind the field. It is a second effect on top of an effect,
so it belongs only where the field is unquestionably the region's focus.

own.name: color
own.doc:
The colour of grid and stars alike: the grid takes `translucency` of it, the stars 70 %. It is a
text role by default so the field follows the theme's ink rather than a fixed white.

own.name: density
own.doc:
How many stars. The cost is paid once, in nodes and in a CSS animation the GPU composites — it
is not a per-frame cost on the main thread, so density is a visual decision rather than a
budget one.

own.name: fade
own.doc:
The elliptical mask that dissolves both layers towards the edges. It is what stops the field
ending in a visible seam where its region does.

own.name: fixed
own.doc: Pins the field to the viewport. `parallax` already does this, so the two rarely go together.

own.name: grid
own.doc: Whether the rule grid is drawn behind the stars.

own.name: gridSize
own.doc: Side of a grid cell, in pixels. Read only with `grid`.

own.name: parallax
own.doc:
Drifts grid and stars at different rates as the page scrolls, and pins the field to the viewport
to do it. It never subscribes on a coarse pointer or under reduced motion: on touch that is a
performance stop, not a preference one.

own.name: scroller
own.doc:
Whose scroll drives the parallax. Left out it listens to the window, which is wrong whenever the
page scrolls inside a container instead of the document — there the field would simply not move.

own.name: seed
own.doc:
Seeds the low-discrepancy sequence the star layout comes from. The layout is generated, never
random, so server and client agree and hydration holds; change this for a different sky at the
same density.

own.name: translucency
own.doc:
The grid's alpha, as a percentage of `color`. ADR-129 pins it at 1 for the page-wide ambient
layer; the default belongs to a hero, where the field is the region's one dominant effect.

own.name: twinkle
own.doc:
Whether the stars pulse. It stops on its own under `prefers-reduced-motion` and under
`motion.tier: "minimal"`, and the field is swapped for an even static one — not frozen wherever
each star happened to be, which would leave some of them invisible.

own.name: children
own.doc:
What animates. They always land inside a `div` this component adds, so a `Transition` between a
flex or grid container and its item inserts a level that breaks the layout.

own.name: className
own.doc: Lands on the animated element, after the classes the style props generate.

own.name: duration
own.doc:
Length of the animation in milliseconds, replacing the theme's `base`. The exit takes two
thirds of it, so it always reads as faster than the entrance. Ignored on the entrance when
`spring` is set.

own.name: mounted
own.doc:
Drives presence. On the way to false the children stay in the DOM until the exit animation
ends, so unmounting the `Transition` itself cuts that animation short. A first render with it
already true does NOT animate in — only later changes do.

own.name: onExitComplete
own.doc:
Fires once the exit has finished and the children have left the DOM — the moment to release
what the content held. It never fires on the entrance.

own.name: spring
own.doc:
Drives the entrance with a theme spring instead of a tween, which leaves `duration` applying to
the exit only. The exit is always a tween: a spring has no fixed end to unmount on.

own.name: style
own.doc:
Inline styles on the animated element; they beat the style props. Do not set `opacity`,
`transform`, `scale`, `x` or `y` here — the animation drives those and will overwrite them.

own.name: transition
own.doc:
Which way it enters and leaves; the exit is the entrance played backwards. Every preset moves
only `transform` and `opacity`, which is what keeps it off the main thread.

own.name: className
own.doc: Composes with the classes `Box` computes instead of replacing them.

own.name: children
own.doc:
The whole of the button. The component strips the browser's appearance but keeps the keyboard,
focus ring and press semantics, so the children carry the entire look — including the visible
focus state, which is the one thing that must not be stripped with it.

own.name: disabled
own.doc:
Blocks the press and stops the hover and focus state being reported. It is a real `button`, so
this also removes it from the tab order — for something that must stay reachable while inert,
mark it `aria-disabled` and guard the handler instead.

own.name: children
own.doc: What renders once the value is valid.

own.name: invalid
own.doc:
What stands in when the value is not valid — an error message, a placeholder, an empty state.
Left out, an invalid value renders nothing.

own.name: valid
own.doc:
Which branch renders. It defaults to false rather than true, so leaving it out renders the
`invalid` branch and never the children.

The element it paints. An inline `span` by default, so the text can sit inside a sentence

browser silently breaks a block element nested in a paragraph.
